title: Monotonic Stack & Deque

views.title: Monotonic Stack, Deque & Parsers
views.intro: A monotonic stack answers "nearest bigger/smaller element" for every index: pop while the new element breaks the order and the pop IS the answer. A monotonic deque keeps the window maximum. A plain stack parses brackets, calculators and nested encodings.
table: Largest rectangle, maximal rectangle, subarray minimums
Sliding window max, shortest subarray with negatives

files.desc: Next greater (plain + circular), daily temps, histogram, maximal rectangle, subarray minimums, remove K digits, stock span, parsers, min stack, sliding max, shortest subarray, limit window

pitfalls: Use strict vs non-strict comparison on exactly one side to avoid double-counting equal elements (sum of subarray minimums).
Append a sentinel 0 height to flush the stack in the histogram problem.
Deque stores indices so expired elements can be dropped from the front.
